evals.prompt: Add an About page to the marketing site. It's small, so put the hero markup and the team list straight into app/(marketing)/about/page.tsx.
evals.expected_output: Should keep page.tsx a thin entry that imports and renders AboutPageContent. Sections go in components/marketing/about/ as named-export files named for the page (AboutHero.tsx, AboutTeam.tsx), composed by index.tsx; the team records go in lib/data/team.data.ts or stay with their section, never in the entry.
expectations: Keeps page.tsx to an import and a render
Creates AboutHero and AboutTeam as named exports
Composes them in an index.tsx exporting AboutPageContent
Keeps data out of the route entry

evals.prompt: Create src/lib/billing/ with hooks.ts, types.ts and utils.ts for the new billing feature.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse a domain folder at the lib/ root: lib/ is kind-first and flat, with the domain as a filename prefix. The files become lib/hooks/use-<subject>.ts, lib/types/billing.type.ts (only if no schema or const already infers the type) and lib/utils/billing.utils.ts, each added to its kind's barrel with one explicit export line.
expectations: Places files by kind with the billing prefix
Uses the <domain>.<kind>.ts grammar and use-<subject>.ts for hooks
Adds one explicit export line per file to each barrel

evals.prompt: Only apps/web uses formatCurrency today, but move it into packages/utils now so it's ready to share.
evals.expected_output: Should keep it in apps/web's lib/utils: consumer count decides placement, and code moves to a package on its second consumer, never before. Should check the project's AGENTS.md first and follow a recorded rule that says otherwise.
expectations: Cites promotion on the second consumer
Checks AGENTS.md for a recorded exception

evals.prompt: In a Client Component I wrote: import { ROUTES } from "@/lib/config". The build now fails with a server-only error. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Should explain that the config barrel is server-only because it re-exports env, which reads secrets, so a client import of the barrel fails the build. The fix is importing the one file by path: import { ROUTES } from "@/lib/config/routes".
expectations: Identifies the config barrel as server-only
Gives the by-path import of routes
